item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 22, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's what's happening across the media industry.
The National Association of Broadcasters has announced its 2026 Marconi Radio Award winners. WBMX in Boston earned Major Market Station of the Year, while Karson and Kennedy won Major Market Personality honors. WIVK in Knoxville was named Legendary Station of the Year, and Julie Koehn of WLEN in Michigan received Legendary Radio Manager of the Year. Houston stations collected three format awards, and Joel Oxley of Hubbard Radio Washington received the NAB National Radio Award for his industry leadership. Read the story and review the complete list of winners at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to podcasts,
A new national podcast study reveals opportunities to increase revenue without adding more commercials. The Podcast Study 2026 found that nearly 55 percent of listeners believe podcasts already carry too many ads. However, 40 percent say host-read endorsements strongly influence purchasing decisions. Researchers also found strong interest in free VIP clubs, premium content, and memberships priced below five dollars monthly. And social media is three times more effective at podcast discovery than advertising within other podcasts. The study surveyed more than 1,200 U.S. podcast consumers and was conducted by Strategic Solutions Research and Point-To-Point Marketing.
In television news,
NBC Universal Media Group Chairman Matt Strauss says live sports, artificial intelligence, and new streaming partnerships are shaping Peacock's future. Speaking at the In the Arena conference, Strauss said Peacock is evolving beyond a streaming service into a broader entertainment platform. NBC Universal reports 225 million Americans watched its major February sports programming, including the Super Bowl and Winter Olympics. The company is also expanding its partnership with YouTube, with a Peacock Premium bundle planned for 2027. Strauss says artificial intelligence and personalized viewing experiences will help drive future audience growth.
Turning to radio,
Audacy's NEW 102.7 raised more than sixteen thousand dollars for VEG Cares during its third annual Anthony's Walk for Animals. Morning show co-host Anthony "Intern Ant" Malerba walked nearly fourteen miles across Staten Island, encouraging listeners to donate. The event also featured support from the Staten Island Tech High School Marching Band. Proceeds help provide emergency veterinary care for pets whose families cannot afford lifesaving treatment.
On the business side of media,
Entravision Communications has appointed former Intel CEO Brian Krzanich and financial executive Gary Ferrera to its Board of Directors. Krzanich brings decades of technology and artificial intelligence experience, while Ferrera has more than 30 years of financial leadership experience. Entravision says the appointments will help accelerate growth in its advertising technology business. Longtime directors Fehmi Zeko and Gilbert Vasquez are also preparing to leave the board.
And finally,
Premiere Networks is bringing country music's biggest stars together for Thanksgiving with the annual *After MidNite Friendsgiving Special*, hosted by Granger Smith. The four-hour program features Luke Bryan, Lauren Alaina, Brothers Osborne, Dustin Lynch, Ella Langley, and Dan + Shay sharing holiday traditions, favorite foods, and personal stories. The barter-free special is available to country radio stations November nineteenth through twenty-ninth. Premiere Networks will also offer a Smith Family Christmas Special beginning December eighteenth.
Stay current with more media news, the latest jobs and free industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
